requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.
requirements.evidence: Cell 0,0,0 half-s base hosts drawer:0#0,0#cut on its north cut face and spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 at junction [0,0|0,1|1,0] which is the north-east corner of that cell. Two neighboring full bases at 0,1,0 and 1,0,0 complete the three-base corner required for the spike, so both sit at the same junction and physically abut.

finish.summary: Placed 3 bases around junction 0,0/0,1/1,0. Replaced 0,0,0 with half-s so its cut faces north into the junction, added spike at that junction, then added drawer key n on the same cell's cut face. Capped open faces and locked joints; mesh clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your drawer and spike share the same corner — I'll set that tight pairing up.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base (variant half-n, half-s, half-e or half-w) first. No place on the build takes this part right now.
